name: EmailListVerify
summary: Email verification with never-expiring pay-as-you-go credits — bulk list cleaning, real-time API, inbox-placement testing and free DMARC/SPF tools, plus a credit-based email finder.
best_for: teams cleaning real sending lists before campaigns: bulk verification at volume rates, with credits that never expire
skip_if: you verify tiny batches occasionally (the entry rate is the worst per-check price), or you mainly want prospecting: the finder burns credits five to ten at a time
honest_knock: The $5 entry pack is the most expensive way to buy: $0.005 per check versus $0.00196 at the 50k tier: a 2.5x spread that rewards guessing your volume upfront. And the email finder quietly consumes 5 credits per found address (10 if you only have the domain), so a 1,000-credit pack finds at most 200 emails, not 1,000. Subscription credits also reset every month, so an unused allowance is simply lost.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-31 on emaillistverify.com/pricing, read from the page's own JSON-LD offer data) Pay-as-you-go credits that never expire: 1,000 for $5 ($0.005/check), 5,000 for $17 ($0.0034), 10,000 for $27 ($0.0027), 25,000 for $54 ($0.00216), 50,000 for $98 ($0.00196), 100,000 for $186 ($0.00186). Monthly subscription at the same volumes: 5,000 for $16 ($0.0032), 10,000 for $25 ($0.0025), 25,000 for $49 ($0.00196), 50,000 for $89 ($0.00178), 100,000 for $168 ($0.00168), 250,000 for $346. The subscription discount runs from 5.9% at 5,000 credits to 9.7% at 100,000, so it grows with volume rather than being a flat rate. API included at every level; the email finder costs 5 credits per address found when a first or last name is supplied and 10 when only a domain is supplied, charged only on a high- or medium-confidence result (confirmed by EmailListVerify support, 24 Sep 2026). Subscription credits reset each billing cycle; unused ones are lost (same source). Free tools: email validator, inbox-placement test, DMARC/SPF generators. Note that /llms.txt and /pricing.md both serve the 404 page under an HTTP 200, so the JSON-LD on the pricing page is the machine-readable source here.

exit_test.what: Uploaded the two-record synthetic example.com kit CSV with several columns. The email column was detected automatically. Deep Scan Recovery was recommended and ON by default: 3 credits/email, up to 6 CR, with total estimated 2–6 CR including Standard. Verification completed within about 1 minute: 2 Invalid MX, 0 safe-to-send; 2 credits deducted, balance 98. No Deep Scan surcharge was observed for this completed run. This synthetic fixture does not measure real-list accuracy or catch-all recovery. Finder used the same balance and advertised 5 credits with a name or 10 for domain only; no lookup performed.
exit_test.awkward: Deep Scan and automatic top-up were both on by default.

sessions.what: We verified a two-row synthetic list on EmailListVerify's free credits on 12 November 2026, read the Email Finder credit rules and opened the pay-as-you-go pricing page. We stopped before paying. We did not download results or test support, invitations or the API.
findings: The account opened with 100 of 100 credits and no card request, matching the '100 free verification credits' claim.
We uploaded a two-row CSV of example.com addresses at 15:00 UTC. The tool found the e-mail column itself ('2 Email addresses to be verified').

The verification window showed Standard at 1 credit per address and Deep Scan Recovery at 3 credits per address, 'Total cost 2 - 6 CR'. Deep Scan was switched on by default and adds up to 30 minutes after Standard. The page says credits are refunded for addresses it cannot resolve.

The list finished in about a minute and cost 2 credits (98 of 100 left). Deep Scan charged nothing because Standard resolved both addresses. Both came back Invalid MX, which is correct because example.com has no mail server.
Email Finder charges 5 credits when a first or last name is given and 10 credits when only a domain is given, from the same balance. We did not run it.

The pricing page preselects pay as you go: 10,000 credits for EUR 27 (EUR 0.0027 per address) and 50,000 for EUR 98 (EUR 0.0020). A monthly plan for 50,000 is EUR 89 a month. The switch 'Automatically buy the same package when your credits run low' was on by default.
The page states prices exclude VAT, with tax calculated at checkout. We did not go past it.
not_tested: Catch-all handling: our synthetic list had no catch-all domain and we used no real addresses
Checkout, tax and the final price
Whether support answers, and what the API and roles allow
